title: Prioritising when everything is a priority: cost of delay and opportunity cost

videos.script: Four pieces of work arrive at Davi's table, and every one of them is the priority. {{title}} Pix in instalments. Seat maps for festivals. An API for partners. And the fix for the seat holds that keep failing on-sales. All four need the same engineers. {{queue}} The usual answers are to pick the most important, to listen to the loudest customer, or to do all four at once. The last one is the most expensive of all, and you will see why. {{parallel}} This lesson puts each item's cost of delay in reais a week. Then it divides by how long the item takes. That ratio is called CD3, and it puts the seat-hold fix first. {{sheet}} Money adds something points cannot. You can add up what a whole order costs. Doing Pix first would cost Coreto one hundred and sixty-two thousand reais more in delay. That number is the opportunity cost, the price of what you chose not to do. {{opportunity}}
